source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, adhyaya 2 (the measure of an akshauhini, told right after Samantapanchaka)
structure: Every episode: RECAP (≈3 s, not in episode 1; KIT.series.recapStrip) → HOOK (one question; the episode title follows it: KIT.series.episodeTitle) → STORY → NEXT (a cliffhanger line, then the teaser card: KIT.series.nextTeaser).

voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice, used by the timeline), say (what is spoken, if not `text`): '…' and '—' pause, ',' and '.' pause a little, [p:400] pauses 400 ms, {s:0.8} speaks what follows at 0.8× until the next {s:…} ({s} resets).

lines.text: Sauti named the battlefield: the field of five lakes.
lines.note: RECAP: episode 2's holy field of five lakes as a memory

lines.speaker: elder_sage
lines.text: You said eighteen armies. How large was one?
lines.note: HOOK. beats[0] = 'How': the elder leans in; the episode title shows in the post

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.text: One chariot, one elephant, three horses, five foot soldiers… that is a patti.
Triple it… then triple that… seven times over.
lines.note: ticks = the seven ×3 steps from 'it' to the line's end (slow and readable first, quicker later), each lighting its ×3 badge; the patti panel shrinks into the first tile before them; beats = 'Triple', 'seven'

lines.text: Then ten times that: one akshauhini. Twenty-one thousand, eight hundred and seventy chariots.
As many elephants. Sixty-five thousand horses. A hundred and nine thousand soldiers on foot.
Eighteen such armies gathered on that field.
And for eighteen days… they fought.
lines.say: And for eighteen days… [p:700] they fought.

lines.text: A war so vast needed a story just as vast. Who first composed it?
lines.note: NEXT (cliffhanger). beats = 'story' (palm leaves rise out of the settling dust), 'Who' (a dark figure with a halo in the mist)
the teaser card, with a glimpse of Ganesha writing

figures.note: Adi Parva 2: a patti (1 chariot, 1 elephant, 3 horses, 5 foot) ×3 senamukha ×3 gulma ×3 gana ×3 vahini ×3 pritana ×3 chamu ×3 anikini ×10 akshauhini. The narration rounds the horses and men; the numerals show the exact figures.
